# Selected cap menus, projected moments, and an exact R4 calibration

This note distinguishes choosing different critical cap rows from
recoupling one fixed profile. It solves an actual nine-cap finite menu
exactly. It also gives a conditional cap-signature diagnostic through
Jensen equality for actual hinge functions. Neither diagnostic is
asserted to hold automatically at a bad attained minimum.

## 1. A finite capacity-transport formulation

Let v_l=(z_l,x_l), l=1,...,N, be finitely many physical points with
positive capacity weights e_l and fixed normal labels n_l. Let H_i,
i=1,...,m, be a finite cap menu, and let

    I_il=1_(v_l in H_i),
    T={theta>=0:sum theta_i=1, sum theta_i b_i=0}

be its actual response polytope, with given scale-invariant response
vectors b_i. Fix a positive normalization beta and put

    mu_l(theta)=(e_l/beta)sum_i theta_i I_il.

The existence of a physical martingale from this source to a submeasure
of the full capacity is exactly the finite linear feasibility problem

    pi_lk>=0, pi_lk=0 if n_l!=n_k,
    sum_k pi_lk=mu_l(theta),
    sum_l pi_lk<=e_k,
    sum_k pi_lk(v_k-v_l)=0 for every l.               (1)

The feasible theta set T_cap is a compact convex polytope: all pi
variables are nonnegative and their total mass is bounded by sum e_l,
and (1) is a closed finite linear system. This is an exact formulation,
not a new lower bound on its complement.

The full projected marginal defect is already fixed by theta:

    d_z(theta)=sum_(l:z_l=z)[e_l-mu_l(theta)].         (2)

Changing pi cannot change (2) or any of its moments. To test projected
closure one must change theta and solve d_z(theta)=0, or establish an
independent zero-moment identity. Merely finding a more favorable
coupling does not address it.

If source and full-capacity masses agree, every feasible pi uses full
capacity. For a positive definite matrix A, its displacement energy is
then the affine function of theta

    E_A(theta)=sum_l [e_l-mu_l(theta)] z_l^T A z_l
              =sum_lk pi_lk (z_k-z_l)^T A(z_k-z_l).   (3)

Thus minimizing this energy over T_cap is a finite LP. A zero optimum
really supplies projected closure; a positive optimum proves that no
feasible selected profile in that menu closes. First moments alone do
not justify substituting zero for (3).

There is also an exact finite selection test: T contains a profile
outside T_cap if and only if some extreme point of T is outside T_cap.
The forward implication follows because a convex set containing every
extreme point contains their convex hull T; the reverse is immediate.
This test repackages the selected-menu problem. Its usefulness requires
actual cap data or a geometric way to solve the finite alternatives.

## 2. The complete nine-cap menu on the actual R4 product

Use the actual product P times K from
`candidate b78a2eb10bd3783f`
and its all-normal dependency
`candidate de93c4f08837e128`, where K
is any triangle of area V and centroid g, and

    P={z in Z^2:ell_i(z)>=-4 for i=0,1,2},
    ell_0=-z1-z2, ell_1=2z1-z2, ell_2=2z2-z1.

There are31 bases. Let lambda_0,lambda_1,lambda_2 be the barycentric
coordinates of K. Take all nine actual caps

    H_ij={lambda_j(x)-1/3+ell_i(z)>=0}, i,j=0,1,2.   (4)

At Y=(0,g), every one has raw mass (40/3)V and is genuinely critical.
This follows from the exact all-normal theorem for the canonical cap
and the independent base and continuous vertex-permutation symmetries.
Every row is regular: its nonproper traces are strictly full or empty,
and its three ell_i=0 traces are proper centroid cuts.

The total coarea factor S_ij is4V, independent of i,j. Indeed a
lambda_j=1/3 section has length/||grad lambda_j||=(2/3)*2V, and
there are three such fibers. Thus the response vector is
4V grad lambda_j. The only linear dependence among the three continuous
gradients has equal coefficients. Consequently the response polytope is

    T={theta_ij>=0: sum_i theta_ij=1/3 for each j}.   (5)

It has27 extreme points, choosing one base index i independently for
each of the three continuous indices j.

Let r_i=sum_j theta_ij be the row sums. On the continuous facet
lambda_k=0 of length L, take eta to be uniform facet length over all
31 bases and mu_theta=(W_theta/beta)eta, beta=40/93. The following
data are obtained directly from the31 base points:

    sum_(ell_0>0)z=(-21,-21),
    sum_(ell_1>0)z=(21,0),
    sum_(ell_2>0)z=(0,21),
    sum_(ell_i=0)z=0 for every i.                    (6)

At ell_i>0 every trace in (4) is full; at ell_i<0 every trace is empty.
At ell_i=0 the relative facet length is zero when j=k and2/3 otherwise.
Since every positive base set has12 points and every zero slice has3,

    mu_theta(total)=(L/beta)[12+2(1-1/3)]=31L,
    integral z d mu_theta=(21L/beta)(r_1-r_0,r_2-r_0). (7)

The full target eta has mass31L and projected first moment zero.
Every martingale to its capacity must therefore use it fully, and (7)
forces r_0=r_1=r_2=1/3.

Conversely, if the row sums are also1/3, the matrix3theta is doubly
stochastic. It is a convex combination of permutation matrices. A
short finite proof is to find a positive perfect matching using the
row/column capacity inequalities, subtract its smallest positive
entry, and iterate after rescaling; at least one positive entry is
removed at each step. The needed matching condition follows because
rows of a subset have their total mass supported on its neighboring
columns, whose total capacity is their cardinality. To prove the
matching assertion directly, choose a matching of maximum cardinality.
If a row is unmatched, follow alternating unmatched and matched edges
starting there. No reachable column can be unmatched, or this path
would augment the matching. The reachable row set S therefore has a
neighbor set of exactly |S|-1 matched columns, contradicting the
capacity condition |neighbors(S)|>=|S|. This is the usual finite proof
of Hall's matching theorem. Subtraction either exhausts the matrix or
leaves equal positive row and column sums, permitting rescaling and
the next step; no zero entry becomes positive, so iteration terminates.

Each permutation profile is a relabeling of the canonical profile by
an actual linear unimodular symmetry of P. Explicitly, for a permutation
pi, define M by ell_(pi(j))(Mz)=ell_j(z). The identities
z1=(ell1-ell0)/3 and z2=(ell2-ell0)/3 show that M and its inverse have
integer entries, so |det M|=1. Push forward its already
certified martingale, preserving the continuous point and normal.
Mixing these actual transports gives the desired martingale for theta.
This works on each continuous facet and hence on their full normal
bundle. We have proved the exact description

    T_cap={theta>=0: every row sum and column sum is1/3}. (8)

Thus T_cap is precisely one third of the3-by3 Birkhoff polytope. Of
the27 extreme response profiles, exactly the six permutation profiles
are transportable. The other21 fail already at projected first moments.
In particular a common-base-tilt selection (one nonzero matrix row)
escapes the capacity cone; this is the same actual favorable selection
that the symmetry theorem pays using an exposed-fiber potential.

Equation (8) is new finite information about this whole menu. It is
not a general theorem that every finite critical menu contains such an
escape, and it does not infer Gamma from a generic failure of (1).

## 3. A positive quadratic defect survives EVERY selected row choice

Define the positive definite quadratic form

    Q(z)=z1^2-z1*z2+z2^2.

It is invariant under the base triangle's vertex permutations. Direct
finite sums give

    sum_(z in P) Q(z)=165,
    sum_(ell_i>0)Q(z)=60,
    sum_(ell_i=0)Q(z)=6 for each i.                  (9)

Using the facet fractions from Section2 and only the column constraints
in (5), every theta in T has

    integral Q(z) d(eta-mu_theta)
      =L[165-(60+8/3)/beta]=(193/10)L>0.            (10)

For every theta in T_cap, the capacity identity makes (10) the exact
Q-displacement energy of EVERY corresponding physical martingale.
Consequently even optimizing theta over the entire transportable menu
cannot close its projection.

There is also a direct projected-marginal obstruction on all of T.
At each of the three outer base vertices, exactly one ell_i is positive
and the other two are negative. Its boundary profile is the constant
r_i. Equality of projected source and full-target marginals at these
three vertices would require r_i=beta for every i, incompatible with
sum r_i=1 because3beta=40/31>1.

Therefore choosing rows can destroy the existence of a capacity
transport, but it cannot produce stationary projection on this menu.
These are genuinely different alternatives. The calibration is above
its OC target and does not rule out a closure theorem that correctly
uses additional bad-minimum hypotheses; it does rule out silently
deriving closure from actual criticality plus row selection alone.

## 4. What exact cap-signature matching would add

There is a precise conditional mechanism, distinct from first-exit
Jensen. Suppose source and target capacity have equal mass and neither
charges the boundary of any menu cap. Let L_i be its affine margin and
F_i=[L_i]_+. For any physical martingale pi, Jensen gives

    J_i=integral F_i d(eta-mu_theta)>=0.             (11)

If J_i=0, almost every transition preserves the sign of L_i. To prove
this, subtract the affine supporting function of F_i at the source.
For a source with positive margin the nonnegative Jensen remainder
is [-L_i(target)]_+; for a negative source it is
[L_i(target)]_+. Zero integral makes these remainders vanish. Boundary
mass is excluded by hypothesis, so signs, rather than merely closed
sides, agree almost everywhere.

It is enough that (11) vanish for every ACTIVE cap, meaning theta_i>0.
The active cap signature is then preserved. On an active-signature
cell sigma, W_theta=theta.sigma is constant.
The source mass in that cell is therefore (theta.sigma/beta) times
its target-capacity mass. Full-capacity signature-preserving transport
forces equality of those masses, so

    W_theta=beta eta-almost everywhere.             (12)

In particular mu_theta=eta as FULL physical measures. The martingale
second-moment identity, applied to all physical coordinates rather than
just z, now yields

    integral ||v'-v||^2 d pi
      =integral ||v||^2 d(eta-mu_theta)=0.

Thus pi is the physical identity almost everywhere. No extra hypothesis
that the signatures distinguish integer bases is necessary. Conversely,
physical identity implies mu_theta=eta and all hinge defects vanish.
Since all J_i are nonnegative, we have the exact equivalences, for a
feasible full-capacity profile on a compact support with the stated
boundary-null hypothesis,

    sum_i theta_i J_i=0
      iff J_i=0 for every active i
      iff mu_theta=eta
      iff pi is physical identity.                (12a)

The equivalence holds for each martingale realizing this fixed profile;
if one is physical identity, the second-moment identity makes all of
them physical identity. Although the individual J_i are affine in
theta, their weighted sum in (12a) is in general quadratic in theta.

The quantities J_i are affine in theta, so zero hinge deficits and
response balance give an exact finite linear test in a finite model
when the proposed active support is fixed (with its positive weights
retained). Equivalently, one may enumerate the finitely many possible
supports and use (12a) on each.
It asks for an actual family of Jensen EQUALITIES, not just matching
first moments or rearranging a coupling. At a putative bad minimum,
one would have to derive those equalities from admissible physical
variations or another theorem. Criticality alone does not do so, and
no such derivation is asserted here.

### The actual R4 menu has strictly positive hinge slack for every choice

For completeness, this conditional test can also be solved on the
transportable R4 menu. Keep the canonical margins in (4), so their
normalization is fixed. On the facet lambda0=0 of length L, for the
canonical permutation profile theta_ij=1_(i=j)/3 the matrix of hinge
defects J_ij/L is exactly

    [ 98/45, 1129/720, 1129/720 ]
    [ 32/9,   707/240, 2183/720 ]
    [ 32/9,  2183/720,  707/240 ].                 (13)

Here J_ij means the integral in (11) with margin
ell_i+lambda_j-1/3. To verify (13), split the facet into its three
equal intervals. On each interval W is constant and every hinge is
affine, because its only possible internal zero occurs at lambda_j=1/3.
Its midpoint value therefore integrates exactly; summing over the31
bases gives the displayed rational entries.

Every permutation response merely permutes the rows in (13), while
arbitrary transportable responses are their convex combinations. Thus
for EVERY theta in T_cap and EVERY one of the nine margins,

    J_ij >= (1129/720)L > 0.                       (14)

The analogous statement holds on the other facets after relabeling.
So neither row selection nor recoupling can produce even a single zero
hinge defect within this transportable menu. This is a calibration of
the missing Jensen-equality premise, not a reason to discard that
premise when trying to derive it at a bad minimum.

## 5. Scope of the finite formulation

Section1 is stated for an actual finite atomic normal-bundle model.
The R4 example is also exact for its continuous facets: its tierwise
finite martingale is carried to the actual points by an affine map
depending on a common parameter r in(0,1), then integrated. It is not
an unproved discretization of an arbitrary convex boundary.

The generic LP is a useful diagnostic but mostly reformulates existing
stress data. Its concrete new content here is the solved feasible
polytope (8), the row-independent positive energy (10), and the
separation between escaping the transport cone and forcing stationary
projection. None supplies the missing general Gamma payment.

The standalone exact verifier
`../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_selected_menu_birkhoff_calibration_defect_transport.py` checks
all 27 response vertices on all three continuous facets directly from
their nine affine cap margins, verifies the integer symmetries, and
pushes the archived rational martingale through all six permutations.
It also checks the nine exact hinge integrals for all six permutation
profiles and all three facets. The Birkhoff argument, not finite
sampling, extends these certificates to every matrix in (8).
